answer: One defense is to make every identity carry a costly, verifiable cipher puzzle bound to a unique hardware attestation, the way no two quartz crystals share the same resonance. An agent must solve a fresh challenge tied to its key before it can transact. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand puzzles, while an honest agent pays once and reuses its proof. Attackers face a steep ledge of rising expense for each extra identity, so the marginal sybil is priced out before it can flood the market.
